ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is an asymptotic magnitude Bode plot, with the vertical axis labeled G(jω)dB, the horizontal axis as frequency ω, and tick marks such as 1, 10, 20, and 100. The slope of the low-frequency section of the broken line is labeled -20 dB/dec; the first break occurs near ω=1, after which the slope becomes -40 dB/dec; the second break occurs near ω=20, after which the slope becomes -60 dB/dec. The low-frequency asymptote corresponds to about 40 dB at ω=1. Reasoning: The initial slope is -20 dB/dec, indicating that the transfer function contains one integrator, so the denominator has a factor s. At ω=1, the slope changes from -20 dB/dec to -40 dB/dec, indicating the addition of a first-order real pole, with factor s+1. At ω=20, the slope changes from -40 dB/dec to -60 dB/dec, indicating the addition of another first-order real pole, with normalized factor 1+s/20=1+0.05s. Let the gain be K; then in the low-frequency section |G(jω)|≈K/ω. From the figure, the magnitude at ω=1 is about 40 dB, so 20log10(K)=40, hence K=100. Combining these gives G(s)=100/[s(s+1)(1+0.05s)].

At the corner omega=20, the slope drops from -40 to -60 dB/dec, so add a real pole at 20 rad/s, written as 1+s/20=1+0.05s. Determine the constant gain from the low-frequency asymptote: near omega=1 before the first break, |G(jomega)|approx K/omega and the plot shows 40 dB, so 20log10K=40 and K=100.
